newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper vulnerable to downside pressure.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper vulnerable to downside pressure.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper prices need to pierce the $2,500 resistance level to look constructive, but technically appear more likely to succumb to selling pressure, analysts said. Key support is at $2,445.
Aluminium is looking more positive on the charts, although a band of resistance at $1,610-$1,620 will be tough.
COPPER - The downside correction which started on Monday could extend, against a background of softening charts and souring sentiment, analyst said.

"Chartwise, the market continues to hold above the $2,460/70 support level but with the 10-day moving average now trending lower, further downside pressure looks inevitable," brokers Brandeis said in a commentary.
Key support is at the recent low of $2,445, and resistance at $2,500 looks to cap the market for now in the absence of upward momentum, it added.
Also weighing on the market is the perception that the steady, healthy drawdowns of LME stocks from earlier this year have come to an end. LME stocks were down just 175 tonnes on Friday.
At 0900 GMT three months copper was at $2,485/$2,490, up slightly from Thursday's kerb close of $2,481.
ALUMINIUM - Diverging from the copper market, aluminium has made forays to the upside this week, thanks to cheerier charts and support from the physical market and LME.
"The recovery has seen repeated challenges of $1,600-plus resistance, which has thus far repelled the metal," said analyst Martin Squires of brokers Rudolf Wolff.
"However, with the technical indicators picking up look for further challenges of overhead resistance at $1,610/20," he added in a commentary.
At 0900 GMT three months aluminium was at $1,596/$1,598 versus $1,600 at the previous kerb close.
